title: Source-to-Recall Gate
user: Students converting highlights into study prompts who need to decide what is worth remembering and encode it as a personally meaningful recall cue before it becomes queue debt.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The discussion distinguishes spaced repetition as retrieval from the separate encoding work required to make knowledge one's own.
A reader who forgets books wants to import highlights but explicitly does not want to memorize paragraphs, exposing the highlight-to-recall design problem.

recurrence: Both threads describe adding material before deciding what the learner can retrieve from it; this routinely produces bloated decks and abandoned review habits.
current_workaround: Dump highlights into Readwise/Notion, import cloze deletions wholesale, or reread passages on a schedule.
incumbents_and_gap: Readwise captures highlights and Anki reviews finished cards; neither imposes a tiny decision gate: why this matters, what cue will retrieve it, and what concrete example proves it.
smallest_useful_product: Browser extension and PWA that saves a selected passage locally, requires one paraphrase, one cue, and one use-case before export as Markdown/CSV/Anki TSV. Non-goals: web scraping, AI-generated cards, cloud highlight sync, or a reader app.
success_measure: In a 30-day cohort, users export fewer than 50% of captured highlights but review 70%+ of those exports at least twice.
monetization: one-time — a local export utility has a clear individual value and no server cost.
constraints: Only user-selected text; no copying of protected books into a service; local storage, clipboard permissions, and clear data deletion.
why_distinct: It deliberately reduces card creation and makes encoding quality visible instead of automating more flashcards.
